news.content: Presented a poster, “AI Cares, But Do I?”: Perceptions of AI-Mediated Empathic Messages from a First-Person Perspective (Han, Lee, Liu, Woodworth, & Hancock), at the UC Davis Communication Horizons conference.

A poster on AI metaphors, “What Is AI Like? Everyday Metaphors, Selective Amplification, and the Limits of Platform Influence on Collective AI Discourse,” was accepted to AEJMC 2026 (Communication Technology Division).
Presented research on building resilience to misinformation and disinformation within the Chinese American diaspora at the Stanford Asian American Research Center Symposium.
The “Going Light” paper received a Best Paper Honorable Mention at CHI 2026.
Invited speaker at the SPSP Pre-Conference on Media and Technology 2026 in Chicago, IL (host: Dr. Gabriella Harari).

The following papers were accepted to ICA 2026 in Cape Town, South Africa:
  • The Role of Agentic Mindsets in Human-AI Collaborative Creativity
  • Going Light: The Effects of Minimal Mobile Phone Adoption on Young Adults’ Well-Being Depend on Motivation
  • Two Faces of Third-Person Perceptions of AI-Generated Content: Disentangling Discernment Efficacy from Presumed Influence
  • Shaping Empathic Messages: How Human-AI Collaboration Influences First-Person Perceptions of Empathy
“Analyzing Adolescents’ Social Media Posts: Insights from Data Donations in Three European Countries” (with Lara Schreurs) was accepted to Mass Communication & Society.
Invited speaker for a fireside conversation at the Digital Wellness Institute, hosted by Dr. Sophie Janicke-Bowles.
Research on metaphors of AI was published in Communications Psychology (Nature).
Research on “workslop” was referenced in connection with Merriam-Webster’s 2025 Word of the Year, “slop.”
Contributed to the Stanford Social Media Lab’s evaluation of Australia’s social media ban and its effects on young people’s mental health, with coverage in BBC, Reuters, and other outlets.
Dissertation research on the overestimation of online toxicity was featured in Vice and Yahoo.
Led a research collaboration with BetterUp on AI-generated “workslop” in the workplace, with coverage in Harvard Business Review, CNN, Axios, Forbes, Fortune, Business Insider, and TechCrunch.
Research on public perceptions of AI was featured in Fortune and Forbes.
Research on misinformation was cited in the National Academies of Sciences report on understanding and addressing misinformation about science.
